Save GHO Observations as an Auditable Data Snapshot

Source: R/data_snapshot.R
data_snapshot.Rd

Wraps an already retrieved GHO data frame with its identity, query context and creation time. It makes no network requests and never fills, rounds, aggregates or otherwise changes observations.

Usage 

data_snapshot(
  data,
  file = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  indicator = NULL,
  backend = NULL,
  scope = NULL,
  key = NULL,
  value_fields = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A data frame returned by gho_data(), or by gho_clean(..., keep_dimensions = TRUE, keep_metadata = TRUE). The default 15-column cleaned output has insufficient identity context. The first schema supports one GHO indicator and one backend per snapshot.

file

Optional local RDS path. Parent directories are created as needed. With NULL, return an in-memory snapshot without writing a file.

source

Optional source identifier. Currently only "gho" is supported. Recorded source information must agree with this argument.

indicator

Optional indicator code, normally read from the data. Supply it for an explicitly declared, empty selection.

backend

Optional "legacy" or "xmart", normally read from Provider / provider or who_provenance. Session options are never used to guess an imported data frame's origin.

scope

Optional, non-empty named list describing the complete query and any local filtering, for example list(area = "PHL", year_from = 2020, year_to = NULL). Names and sets of values are canonicalized for comparison. With NULL, use the recorded request URL or xMart table/filter from a complete DSIR retrieval whose recorded row count still matches data. After local subsetting, supply an explicit scope; do not infer query limits from observed coverage.

key

Optional additional semantic identity columns. Required GHO identity and dimension columns are always included. This argument can resolve a genuinely additional dimension, not hide duplicate observations.

value_fields

Optional fields classified as values. Defaults to numeric value, bounds and the original display value, when present. The primary numeric field is always required.

overwrite

Logical. Replace an existing file? Default FALSE.

Value

The snapshot, invisibly when written to file and visibly otherwise.

Details

The result is an ordinary R list, classed dsir_data_snapshot, with schema_version = 1L, created_at (UTC POSIXct), source, backend, indicator, layout, origin, scope, provenance, retrieved_at, source_timestamp_fields, key, value_fields, primary_value, context_fields and the complete, unmodified data frame. Read a saved snapshot with readRDS(). This is distinct from snapshot(), which caches an expression and returns its value without this comparison contract.

Default identity includes indicator, geographical type/code, temporal type/value, all positional dimension type/code pairs and every named DIM_* (or cleaned dim_*) column. Available detailed time coordinates, unit and measure family also participate. A legacy data-source dimension is identity; xMart's free-text source provenance is metadata. Row numbers, service record IDs and modification timestamps are not matching keys. Duplicate keys, untyped active dimensions and missing core identifiers are errors. An inactive dimension may have both type and code missing.

Four different times must remain separate:

  • Source modification time: a provider-reported field, if supplied. Date / updated is preserved verbatim. Its presence does not establish an authoritative observation revision time; xMart system commits can reflect processing.

  • Retrieval time: the original DSIR who_provenance$retrieved string (recorded in UTC by the clients), or NA when unavailable.

  • Snapshot creation time: when this wrapper was made, explicitly UTC.

  • Latest observation year: a property of the data, never an update time.

Only information present in the supplied frame and declared arguments is recorded. No credentials, environment variables, session options or HTTP request objects are collected. Credential-like field names, authenticated URLs and unsupported objects are rejected. Callers remain responsible for checking their own free-text observations and metadata before saving.

A declared scope is an auditable caller assertion, not proof of completeness. Local edits that preserve the original row count cannot be detected from provenance alone. Always declare a new scope after changing selection. Snapshots record what DSIR returned; fields already discarded upstream or by a cleaner cannot be recovered. No content hash is used: comparison operates on keys and values rather than R serialization bytes.

See also

compare_snapshots(), snapshot(), gho_data(), gho_last_updated().

Examples 

x <- data.frame(
  IndicatorCode = "EXAMPLE", SpatialDimType = "COUNTRY",
  SpatialDim = "PHL", TimeDimType = "YEAR", TimeDim = 2020L,
  Dim1Type = "SEX", Dim1 = "SEX_BTSX",
  Dim2Type = NA_character_, Dim2 = NA_character_,
  Dim3Type = NA_character_, Dim3 = NA_character_, NumericValue = 10
)
old <- data_snapshot(x, backend = "legacy",
                     scope = list(area = "PHL", year_from = 2020))
x$NumericValue <- 12
new <- data_snapshot(x, backend = "legacy",
                     scope = list(area = "PHL", year_from = 2020))
compare_snapshots(old, new)$modified

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
old_data <- gho_data("WHS4_100")
data_snapshot(old_data, file = "snapshots/gho_old.rds")

# Later, repeat exactly the same query using the same backend.
new_data <- gho_data("WHS4_100")
data_snapshot(new_data, file = "snapshots/gho_new.rds")
result <- compare_snapshots("snapshots/gho_old.rds",
                            "snapshots/gho_new.rds")
result$summary
result$modified
} # }
